hub.title: Shopinbos vs Bumpa, Selar, Jumia, Shopify and more (2026)
hub.description: Honest, sourced comparisons of Shopinbos with Nigerian store builders, marketplaces, global builders and social selling: prices, fees, pay on delivery and delivery.
hub.lead: Side-by-side comparisons with the other ways Nigerians sell online. Real prices with sources, what each one does well, and when another option suits you better.

groups.label: Nigerian store builders
groups.lead: Apps made in Nigeria for running an online shop.

groups.label: Nigerian marketplaces
groups.lead: Big shopping sites where you list next to other sellers.

groups.label: Global store builders
groups.lead: International website and shop builders, mostly priced in dollars.

groups.label: Social selling
groups.lead: Selling straight from your social apps.

faq: Which is the best online store builder in Nigeria?

It depends on how you sell. If you sell physical products to customers in Nigeria and want pay on delivery, riders and suppliers in one app, Shopinbos is built for that. If you sell courses or e-books, Selar is strong. If you sell to many countries, a global builder like Shopify may fit better. Each page here lists the strengths of both sides.
Are these prices up to date?
We checked every price on 30 October 2026 and link to the source. Prices change, so check the provider's own site before you pay.
Can I use Shopinbos together with Jumia, Instagram or WhatsApp?
Yes. Many sellers list on a marketplace and also run their own store. Shopinbos works alongside Instagram, WhatsApp and TikTok: you share your store and product links there.

us.name: Shopinbos
us.short: Online store, pay on delivery, delivery partners and Nigerian suppliers in one app.

price: Free plan (₦0), Starter ₦6,000, Growth ₦18,000, Pro ₦40,000 a month. Yearly plans give 2 months free.
fee: 3% (Free), 2% (Starter), 1% (Growth) or 0.5% (Pro) on each store sale, plus Paystack's card fee.
pod: Yes, on Growth and Pro. The customer pays the shop at the door from their payment link or the rider's QR code (through Paystack), then gives the delivery code.
naira: Yes. Plans and prices in naira. Card, transfer and USSD through Paystack, paid out to your bank.
delivery: Yes. Book delivery partners in the app, offer self-pickup or doorstep delivery at checkout, and track every delivery.
social: Share your store and product links on WhatsApp, Instagram and TikTok. Chats come into one inbox, and you can sync a WhatsApp catalogue.
domain: Free name.mybos.store address on every plan. Your own domain from Starter.
sourcing: Yes. Registered sellers can find stock from Nigerian suppliers, dropship it or order wholesale.
ai: Rex builds your store from a chat. Peggy drafts replies to customers.
app: Web app; phone app in pilot
Shopinbos Business runs in your phone's browser. The phone app is in pilot.

us.pricing_note: Paystack's card fee also applies to card payments. Pay on delivery is on Growth and Pro. VAT is added where it applies.
pros: Built for selling in Nigeria: naira prices, Paystack payments and payouts to your bank
Pay on delivery without riders handling cash (Growth and Pro)
Book delivery partners and track deliveries in the same app
Find stock from Nigerian suppliers, dropship or buy wholesale
Free plan to start, and AI helpers (Rex and Peggy)
cons: New: a younger company with a shorter track record than most names here
The phone app is still in pilot; most sellers use it in the browser
Nigeria-focused: not the best choice if you mostly sell abroad
Pay on delivery is only on Growth and Pro
Fewer themes and add-ons than the big global builders

bumpa.name: Bumpa
bumpa.short: Nigerian app for running a business: website, inventory, in-store sales and bookkeeping.
bumpa.answer: Bumpa is a strong choice if you run a physical shop and want inventory, in-store checkout and bookkeeping in one app. Shopinbos suits sellers who mainly sell online and on social media and want pay on delivery, delivery partners and Nigerian suppliers built in. Both price in naira; Bumpa bills by the quarter or year, Shopinbos by the month or year and has a free plan.

price: Starter ₦15,000 a quarter (about ₦5,000 a month), Pro ₦30,000 a quarter. Growth and Scale are billed every 6 or 12 months. 14-day free trial.
fee: Not shown on their pricing page. Check their site for payment fees.
pod: Not mentioned on their pricing page. Check their site.
naira: Yes. Naira payments, and dollars too; Growth and up can show prices in NGN, USD, CAD and GBP.
delivery: Shipping rates on every plan. Automated shipping, pick-up locations and tracking on Pro and up.
social: Not listed on their pricing or home page. Check their site.
domain: Buy a domain on Starter. A free .com.ng on Pro and up.
ai: No AI tools listed on their home page.
app: Yes, on Google Play and the App Store.

plans: ₦15,000 a quarter · ₦28,000 for 6 months · ₦55,000 a year
₦30,000 a quarter · ₦55,000 for 6 months · ₦105,000 a year

Several locations and staff accounts on higher plans
Phone apps on Google Play and the App Store

No free plan listed after the trial

faq: Is Bumpa or Shopinbos better for Nigerian sellers?

Bumpa is strong for physical shops that need inventory, in-store checkout and bookkeeping. Shopinbos is built for selling online and on social media, with pay on delivery, delivery partners and Nigerian suppliers. Choose by how most of your sales happen.
How much does Bumpa cost?

On 30 October 2026 Bumpa's Starter plan was ₦15,000 a quarter (about ₦5,000 a month) and Pro was ₦30,000 a quarter, with longer plans for Growth and Scale. Check getbumpa.com/pricing for today's prices.
Is Shopinbos free?
Shopinbos has a Free plan with a 3% fee on each sale. Paid plans start at ₦6,000 a month and lower the fee to as little as 0.5%.

selar.name: Selar
selar.short: Nigerian platform for selling digital products, courses, memberships and tickets.
selar.answer: For e-books, online courses, memberships and event tickets, Selar is usually the better fit: it is built for creators and takes many currencies. For physical products delivered in Nigeria, Shopinbos fits better because pay on delivery, delivery partners and Nigerian suppliers are built in. Both have a free plan.

fee: 4% + ₦50 on each naira sale. You can ask the buyer to pay it.

delivery: You can sell physical products, but delivery is up to you.
social: Share product links anywhere, including WhatsApp and Instagram.
domain: Custom domain on Pro and up.
ai: No AI tools listed on their pricing page.

pricing.currency: Naira (also priced in USD and other currencies)
pricing.note: Selling fee on naira sales: 4% + ₦50 per sale (Selar help centre). Quarterly and yearly plans cost less per month.

Made for digital products: e-books, courses, memberships, tickets and bookings
Sells in many currencies, good for buyers abroad
Affiliates, coupons, upsells and sales pages
cons: Physical delivery is up to you
No pay on delivery
A 4% + ₦50 fee on each naira sale, on every plan we checked
No supplier marketplace

Selar is better for digital products and courses. Shopinbos is better for physical products delivered in Nigeria, with pay on delivery and delivery partners built in.
What does Selar charge per sale?
Selar's help centre says it charges 4% + ₦50 on each naira sale, and you can pass this to the buyer. Check selar.com for other currencies.
Can I sell digital products on Shopinbos?
Shopinbos is built mainly for physical products. If digital products are your main business, Selar is likely the better fit.
sources: Selar help centre: passing transaction fees to customers

paystack-storefront.name: Paystack Storefront
paystack-storefront.short: A simple shop page inside your Paystack account.
paystack-storefront.answer: Paystack Storefront is a quick, simple way to take payments for a few products if you already use Paystack. Shopinbos is a full online store with pay on delivery, delivery partners and suppliers, and it also takes payments through Paystack. Start with Storefront if you need something simple today; move to Shopinbos when you want to run the whole shop.

price: No separate subscription; you need a Paystack account.
fee: Paystack's normal fees. Their published local rate is 1.5% + ₦100 (₦100 waived under ₦2,500), capped at ₦2,000. Check paystack.com.
naira: Yes. You can make storefronts in different currencies too.
delivery: Set delivery fees by location and collect addresses. You arrange the delivery.
social: Share your store link anywhere, and add your social links.
domain: Your store lives on a Paystack link.

pricing.note: The local rate above is Paystack's long-standing published rate. Check paystack.com/ng/pricing for today's rate.

No extra subscription
Discounts, delivery fees by location and several storefronts
Paystack's trusted checkout
cons: A simple shop page, not a full store with themes and pages
No pay on delivery
You arrange delivery yourself
No own domain, inbox or supplier marketplace

You want a payment page today with no subscription
You don't need delivery or pay on delivery
choose_us: You want a full store with your own domain

faq: Is Paystack Storefront or Shopinbos better for Nigerian sellers?

Storefront is great for taking payments quickly with no subscription. Shopinbos is a full store with pay on delivery, delivery partners and suppliers. Many sellers start simple and move when orders grow.
Is Paystack Storefront still available?
Yes. Paystack's help centre still explains how to create and edit a Storefront (checked 30 October 2026).
Does Shopinbos use Paystack?
Yes. Card, transfer and USSD payments on Shopinbos go through Paystack and are paid out to your bank.

flutterwave-store.name: Flutterwave Store
flutterwave-store.short: A free online store from Flutterwave, listed on Flutterwave Market.
flutterwave-store.answer: Flutterwave Store is a free, simple way to list products and take payments, and your store appears on Flutterwave Market. Shopinbos is a fuller store with pay on delivery, delivery partners and Nigerian suppliers built in. If you only need a product page and payments, Flutterwave Store is enough; if you want to run deliveries and orders in one place, Shopinbos fits better.

fee: Flutterwave's local rate: 2% per payment (1.4% + 0.6% platform fee), plus VAT. Customers pay it by default.

domain: Your store lives on a Flutterwave link.

Variants, discounts and low-stock alerts
Takes local and international payments

Flutterwave Store is a good free start for taking payments. Shopinbos suits sellers who want pay on delivery, delivery partners and a full store with their own domain.
Is Flutterwave Store still running?
Yes. Flutterwave's Nigeria site still offers Store and says it is free to set up (checked 30 October 2026).
Who pays Flutterwave's fee?
Flutterwave's pricing page says customers bear the transaction charges by default, and you can change that.

jumia.name: Jumia
jumia.short: One of Nigeria's biggest online marketplaces, with its own delivery.
jumia.answer: Jumia gives you access to a very large group of shoppers and handles delivery, but you pay commission on each sale and sell next to many other sellers. Shopinbos gives you your own store, your own customers and lower fees per sale, but you bring the shoppers yourself. Many sellers use both.

price: Free to register, per Jumia's vendor pages. You pay commission on sales.
fee: Commission on each sale, set by category, plus other fees and VAT. Check Jumia Seller Center for today's rates.
pod: Shoppers can choose pay on delivery, with limits on some items and places.
social: Shoppers buy on Jumia, not in your chats.
app: Big shopper app; seller tools in Seller Center.

pricing.note: Jumia's vendor guide shows a 5% commission as an example, not a fixed rate. Fines apply for counterfeit items.

Your products sell well on price
choose_us: You want your own brand and your own customers
You sell through WhatsApp, Instagram or TikTok
You want lower fees per sale
faq: Is Jumia or Shopinbos better for Nigerian sellers?
Jumia is better for reaching shoppers fast without your own following. Shopinbos is better for building your own brand with your own customers and lower fees per sale. Many sellers do both.
How much commission does Jumia charge?
Jumia sets commission by category and changes it from time to time. Check Jumia Seller Center for today's rates.
Can I sell on Jumia and Shopinbos at the same time?
Yes. You can keep your Jumia listings and run your own Shopinbos store for repeat customers.

konga.name: Konga
konga.short: Long-running Nigerian marketplace with KongaPay and its own delivery.
konga.answer: Konga puts your products in front of shoppers who already use it, with KongaPay and Konga's delivery. You pay commission and compete with other sellers on the same page. Shopinbos gives you your own store and customers, with pay on delivery and delivery partners, for a monthly plan and a smaller fee per sale.

Konga is better for reaching marketplace shoppers. Shopinbos is better for your own brand, your own customers and selling on social media. Many sellers use both.

Yes. Konga.com was live with a Sell on Konga sign-up when we checked on 30 October 2026.
How much does Konga charge sellers?
Konga charges commission by category. Check Konga SellerHQ or its seller handbook for today's rates.

jiji.name: Jiji
jiji.short: Nigeria's big classifieds site: post ads and buyers contact you.
jiji.answer: Jiji is great for reaching lots of buyers with free ads, especially for phones, cars, property and used items, and it takes no commission. But there is no checkout: you agree payment and delivery with each buyer yourself. Shopinbos gives you a store with checkout, pay on delivery and delivery partners, so orders run in one place.

price: Basic ads are free. Paid boosts and premium packages give more views.
fee: No commission on sales; Jiji earns from paid boosts.
pod: No checkout. You agree payment with each buyer.

Jiji is better for free ads and one-off or used items. Shopinbos is better if you sell regularly and want checkout, pay on delivery and delivery in one place.
Does Jiji charge commission?
No. Basic ads are free and Jiji earns from paid boosts and premium packages.
Can I post my Shopinbos products on Jiji?
Yes. You can post ads on Jiji and send buyers to your Shopinbos store link to order.
sources: Jiji help: WhatsApp contact and safety

shopify.name: Shopify
shopify.short: The world's best-known store builder, priced in dollars.
shopify.answer: Shopify is excellent if you sell to many countries or need its huge app store, and you are happy to pay in dollars. For selling mainly in Nigeria, Shopinbos is simpler and cheaper to start: naira plans, pay on delivery, delivery partners and Nigerian suppliers are built in, where Shopify needs apps. Shopify Payments isn't offered in Nigeria, so you'd add Paystack and pay Shopify's extra fee.

price: Basic $27, Grow $72, Advanced $399 a month (less if billed yearly). Billed in US dollars.
fee: Shopify Payments isn't offered in Nigeria, so Shopify adds 2% (Basic), 1% (Grow) or 0.6% (Advanced) on top of your payment provider's fee.

naira: Yes, with the Paystack app. Your store prices must be in naira.
delivery: Through third-party apps. No Nigerian riders built in.
social: Sales channels and apps; check which work in Nigeria.
ai: Shopify Magic and Sidekick AI tools.

Shopify is better for selling worldwide and for its app store. Shopinbos is better for selling in Nigeria, with naira plans, pay on delivery and delivery partners built in.
Is Shopify available in Nigeria?
Yes, you can use Shopify from Nigeria and take naira payments with the Paystack app. Shopify Payments isn't offered in Nigeria, so Shopify adds its own fee on each sale.
How much is Shopify in naira?
Shopify Basic was $27 a month on 30 October 2026, about ₦36,000 at the market rate that day. Your bank's card rate may be higher.

wix.name: Wix
wix.short: Popular drag-and-drop website builder with online store plans.
wix.answer: Wix is a great website builder with lots of design freedom, and it can take naira payments through Paystack. But it is billed in dollars, and delivery, pay on delivery and suppliers are not built for Nigeria. Shopinbos is the simpler, cheaper choice if you mainly sell products in Nigeria; Wix suits you if the website and design matter most.

Can Wix take naira payments?
Yes. Wix's help centre lists Paystack as a payment provider for Nigeria.
How much is Wix in Nigeria?
Wix's Core plan, the cheapest that takes payments, was $29 a month billed yearly on 30 October 2026 (US price), about ₦39,000. Wix prices vary by country.

woocommerce.name: WooCommerce
woocommerce.short: Free, open-source shop plugin for WordPress websites.
woocommerce.answer: WooCommerce is free, flexible and lets you own everything, with Paystack and cash on delivery available. Shopinbos is ready to sell from day one with pay on delivery, delivery partners and suppliers built in.

fee: WooCommerce takes no cut. You pay your payment provider, such as Paystack.

Can I move from WooCommerce to Shopinbos?

instagram-shop.short: Selling through your Instagram page, posts and DMs.
instagram-shop.answer: Instagram is where many Nigerian shoppers find products, and it costs nothing to post. Shopinbos doesn't replace Instagram: it gives your followers a store link to order and pay, with pay on delivery and delivery handled.

naira: Customers pay by transfer or a link you send.

Can I sell directly on Instagram in Nigeria?
You can post products and take orders in DMs. Instagram's in-app checkout depends on country; check Meta's eligibility rules.
Does Shopinbos work with Instagram?
Yes. Share your store and product links on Instagram, and bring your Instagram chats into the Shopinbos inbox.

faq: Is WhatsApp Business or Shopinbos better for Nigerian sellers?
Use both. WhatsApp is where you chat; Shopinbos is where customers order and pay, and where you track deliveries. Send your store link in chats instead of screenshots.
Can customers pay inside WhatsApp in Nigeria?
Not that we could confirm. Most sellers ask for a transfer or send a payment link. Shopinbos payment links go through Paystack.
Can I use my WhatsApp catalogue with Shopinbos?
Yes. You can add products from your WhatsApp catalogue and sync your Shopinbos products to a WhatsApp catalogue.

woocommerce-vs-shopify.title: WooCommerce vs Shopify for Nigerian sellers: pricing, pros and cons (2026)
woocommerce-vs-shopify.description: WooCommerce or Shopify for a small business in Nigeria? Real prices, Paystack fees, pros and cons, checked 30 October 2026.
woocommerce-vs-shopify.h1: WooCommerce vs Shopify for Nigerian sellers
woocommerce-vs-shopify.answer: WooCommerce is free to install and takes no cut of your sales, but you pay for hosting and handle setup and updates yourself. Shopify is easier and runs everything for you, but it is billed in dollars and adds an extra fee on each sale in Nigeria because Shopify Payments isn't offered here. Pick WooCommerce for control and lower running fees; pick Shopify for ease.
faq: Is WooCommerce cheaper than Shopify in Nigeria?
Often, yes. WooCommerce takes no cut, while Shopify charges a monthly plan in dollars plus 2% to 0.6% on each sale when you use Paystack. Hosting and plugins for WooCommerce cost extra, though.
Which is easier for a beginner?
Shopify. It handles hosting, security and updates. WooCommerce needs more setup, often with a developer.
Is there an option built for Nigeria?
Shopinbos is built for Nigerian sellers, with naira plans, pay on delivery and delivery partners. See Shopinbos vs WooCommerce and Shopinbos vs Shopify.
